Modified by Faithful Ferret.

The files in this folder are test data for the Bitwarden import. They are made up: every
name, address, user name, password, one-time password seed and number in them is invented,
and none belongs to a real account. A JSON file cannot carry a header of its own, so this
notice covers all of them.

Their shapes (the keys, the numbers of the item types, the field types and the address match
rules, and how the CSV holds custom fields and addresses) follow the examples and tests of
Bitwarden:

  every-type.json, small.json, schemes.json, hostile.json, huge-depth.json
      the Bitwarden SDK, crates/bitwarden-exporters/src/json.rs, and the Bitwarden clients,
      libs/importer/src/importers/spec-data/bitwarden-json/unencrypted.json.ts
  encrypted.json, password-protected.json
      the Bitwarden clients, libs/importer/src/importers/spec-data/bitwarden-json/
      account-encrypted.json.ts and password-protected.json.ts (the values are replaced
      with text that is not an encrypted string)
  passkeys.json (and ../passkeys-expected.json)
      the Bitwarden clients, libs/common/src/models/export/fido2-credential.export.ts, and the
      Bitwarden SDK, crates/bitwarden-fido (the keys are throwaway P-256 keys made for these
      tests, for the site rp-a.test, and registered nowhere)
  small.csv
      the Bitwarden SDK, crates/bitwarden-exporters/src/csv.rs, and the Bitwarden clients,
      libs/importer/src/importers/bitwarden/bitwarden-csv-importer.spec.ts

Origin: https://github.com/bitwarden/sdk-internal and https://github.com/bitwarden/clients,
